# `adt fetch`

Fetch a URL with authentication (like curl but authenticated)

```bash
adt fetch [options] <url>
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | Description                                              | Default |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `<url>`  | URL path to fetch (e.g., /sap/bc/adt/core/http/sessions) |         |

**Options**

| Option                  | Description                                                 | Default |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `-X, --method <method>` | HTTP method                                                 | `GET`   |
| `-H, --header <header>` | Add header (can be used multiple times)                     | `[]`    |
| `-d, --data <data>`     | Request body (for POST/PUT)                                 |         |
| `-o, --output <file>`   | Save response to file                                       |         |
| `--accept <type>`       | Set Accept header (shorthand for -H "Accept: &lt;type&gt;") |         |

Global options (`--sid`, `--config`, `--verbose`, …) are accepted by every command — see the [command reference index](./index.md#global-options).
